description: A reusable policy for rehearsing an interpersonal or professional performance with a simulated person (a standardized or virtual patient, a simulated client, customer or colleague, avatar or simulated students, a pedagogical agent, or an AI role-play partner): name the performance and how it will be judged, give novices an example first, run short repeated encounters with feedback and a debrief after each, vary and harden the scenarios across sessions, and judge the unit on a blinded performance with a different person rather than on in-simulation scores or satisfaction.
title: Practice with Simulated People

description: A reusable policy for problem-centred units: establish what learners already know of the target content, guide novices explicitly, use a problem-first phase only where learners can generate partial solutions and instruction follows, and judge the unit on individual outcomes.
title: Problem-Based Learning

description: A reusable policy for teachers: one observable classroom practice is modelled, rehearsed, enacted with the teacher's own students and given feedback in coaching cycles over a term, with support faded and use checked later; expected to change observed practice where the target is specific and coach time is sustained, though no claim here compares it with one-off workshops.
title: Professional Development

description: A reusable sequence in which content is broken into small frames, each needing an active response that is confirmed or corrected at once, with progress at the learner's pace or by branching on the response, behind a unit check; expected to help with facts, rules and procedures that have checkable answers when steps fit prior knowledge and a dated schedule guards against non-completion. No claim in this wiki tests programmed instruction itself; the nearest evidence is from self-paced mastery programs (PSI), feedback after retrieval and intelligent tutoring.
title: Programmed Instruction

description: A reusable policy in which learners work on an authentic project, pause it at a diagnosed gap in a component skill, practise that skill in a separate instructional space to an explicit criterion and then resume the project; expected to improve individual mastery and transfer where gaps can be diagnosed and instruction delivered, but no claim in this wiki tests the design as a whole.
title: Project Space and Instructional Space
